# MODULE / MORNING — client facts

## Client and scope

- Project name: MODULE / MORNING.
- Printed phrase: Two modules, shifting positions.
- Product: expressive modular brooch for tailored wool and softer casual layers.
- Audience: adults moving between formal and everyday clothing; shape language independent of gender labels.
- Designed object inventory: exactly two decorative modules, D1 and D2, plus their designed detachable link.
- Solo compatibility: D1 on P or C; D2 on P or C.
- Pair compatibility: D1+D2 on P or C.
- Paired support: one carrier attached to one module; the second module supported through the detachable link.
- Scope: decorative modules and their link; supplied garments and carriers retained.

## Supplied carrier interface — all dimensions in millimetres

| Carrier | Type | Garment thickness | Flat mounting plate | Closed rear projection from mounting face | Existing mechanism features |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P | Pin carrier | 1.5–3.0 mm | 24 × 6 × 2 mm | 7 mm | Needle covered by catch when closed |
| C | Non-piercing clip carrier | 0.6–1.2 mm | 28 × 8 × 2 mm | 9 mm | Opening clip jaw; supplied soft pads on garment contact faces |

- Plate holes: two M2 threaded mounting holes per carrier.
- Hole centre spacing: 12 mm along the plate's long axis.
- Hole centres in local mounting-face coordinates: (−6, 0) and (+6, 0).
- Fixed interface: attachment face and hole positions.
- Module mounting: two corresponding clearance holes per module, diameter 2.4 mm, with access for two supplied M2 screws.
- Common module-back accommodation: C mounting footprint, 28 × 8 mm, for either carrier choice.
- Carrier exchange: supplied screws removed with a screwdriver; tool access with jewellery removed from clothing.
- Screw length and thread engagement: open engineering dimensions.
- D1–D2 link operation: attachment and detachment by hand.
- Paired mounting clearance: each module's mounting holes clear of the other module's material.
- Mechanism clearances: closed needle catch, clip jaw opening and soft garment pads clear of decorative parts.
- Link construction options: integral tabs, slots or formed features in the module materials.
- Purchased connection inventory: P, C and supplied M2 screws.

## Decorative envelope and materials

| Object | Maximum decorative bounding box | Measurement scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | 35 × 35 × 4 mm | Module excluding carrier |
| D2 | 35 × 35 × 4 mm | Module excluding carrier |
| D1+D2 | 70 × 45 × 4 mm | Complete decorative pair excluding carrier, every displayed arrangement |

- Exact decorative dimensions: design choice within the bounding boxes.
- Bounding-box function: geometric envelope.
- Decorative material palette: M1 and/or M2.

| Material ID | Material | Sheet thickness | Colour | Surface options |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| M1 | Uncoated 316L stainless steel sheet | 1.0 mm | Natural stainless steel | Brushed; optional directional brushing |
| M2 | Through-coloured acrylic sheet | 2.0 mm | Designer-selected solid colour | Matte or polished |

- Layering: permitted within 4 mm total decorative depth.
- Material IDs: design labels.
- Specification data: material IDs, sheet thicknesses, colour names or codes, finish allocation.
- Exposed decorative edges: softened.
- Clothing and skin contact geometry: softened surfaces and points.

## Wearing conditions

- Wearers: adults.
- Body presentation: varied adult bodies; model identity open.
- Crop content: named clothing location, attachment and readable jewellery scale.
- Wearing-board labels: W number, module configuration, carrier ID and fabric thickness.
- Wearing-board inset: one small reverse/contact view identifying the carrier.
- Jewellery depiction: selected modules attached at the recorded clothing location, with consistent relative scale.
- Image variables: lighting, clothing colour and camera framing.

| Record | Module configuration | Clothing location | Fabric thickness | Carrier | Arrangement relationship |

| W01 | D1+D2 | Left wool-jacket lapel | 2.4 mm | P | Initial lapel pair arrangement |
| W02 | D1 alone | Scarf edge | 0.8 mm | C | Solo D1 |
| W03 | D2 alone | Right wool-jacket lapel | 2.4 mm | P | Solo D2 |

| W07 | D1+D2 | Right wool-jacket lapel | 2.4 mm | P | Pair rotated from W01; module shapes unchanged |
| W08 | D2 alone | Shirt placket | 1.0 mm | C | Solo D2 |
| W09 | D1+D2 | Cardigan pocket edge | 1.1 mm | C | Different allowed pair arrangement from W04 |
| W10 | D1 alone | Cardigan pocket edge | 1.1 mm | C | Solo D1 |

## Image context

- carrier-and-wearing-constraints.png: fixed carrier mounting faces, clearance-hole coordinates, decorative envelope limits and W01–W10 records.
- wearer-wardrobe.png: recurring wool jacket, scarf, shirt and cardigan, worn by an adult; garment identity and placement landmarks.
- everyday-materials.png: brushed metal, solid-colour acrylic and neutral wardrobe textures; atmosphere reference.

steps.userMessage:
MODULE / MORNING | Two modules for changing clothes and occasions

We are commissioning a modular brooch system for adults who move between tailored wool and softer everyday layers. The designed objects are two decorative modules, D1 and D2, and their detachable link. Each module works alone on either supplied carrier; the pair also works on either carrier, with one carrier attached to one module and the second module supported through the link. We want an expressive shape language that carries across these changes of position. Print "MODULE / MORNING" and "Two modules, shifting positions" on the final system drawing and on the presentation cover where one is delivered.

The supplied carriers set the rear interface. P serves fabric 1.5–3.0 mm thick: its mounting plate is 24 × 6 × 2 mm and its closed mechanism projects 7 mm behind the mounting face. C serves fabric 0.6–1.2 mm thick: its plate is 28 × 8 × 2 mm and its closed mechanism projects 9 mm behind the mounting face. Both have two M2 threaded holes at 12 mm centre spacing, with centres at (−6, 0) and (+6, 0). Each module needs corresponding 2.4 mm clearance holes, room for the larger C footprint and screwdriver access when removed from clothing. Carrier changes use the supplied screws; the D1–D2 link attaches and detaches by hand. Preserve the covered needle catch, opening clip jaw and soft contact pads, with mounting holes clear of the other module in paired arrangements.

Each module fits within 35 × 35 × 4 mm; every displayed decorative pair fits within 70 × 45 × 4 mm, excluding the carrier. Choose the actual dimensions. The decorative palette is M1, uncoated brushed 316L stainless steel sheet, 1.0 mm thick, and/or M2, through-coloured acrylic sheet, 2.0 mm thick. Allocate the materials and finishes explicitly, soften exposed edges and use integral features for the link. The wearing range moves from a 2.4 mm wool lapel to a 0.8 mm scarf edge, a 1.0 mm shirt placket and a 1.1 mm cardigan pocket edge.

Audience: adults choosing accessories for formal and everyday clothing, with our studio and workshop using the work to select the range and develop its construction.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the carrier dimensions, material records and W01–W10 wearing conditions. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists each deliverable's proportion, format and stage. carrier-and-wearing-constraints.png maps the fixed mounting geometry, decorative envelopes and wearing records. wearer-wardrobe.png supplies the recurring jacket, scarf, shirt and cardigan identities for the wearing images. everyday-materials.png supplies the atmosphere of brushed metal, solid-colour acrylic and neutral clothing textures.

Deliverables:
1. Three distinct direction boards, one per direction, each with D1, D2 and a paired view exploring a different silhouette and link arrangement within the supplied interfaces
2. One selection note naming one of the three directions and explaining the choice through its solo proportions, paired proportions and connection layout
3. One one-page materials and craft note for the selected direction, stating actual module and pair dimensions, material IDs and thicknesses, colour and finish allocations, edge treatment and link construction
4. One final system drawing with D1 and D2 front, rear and side views and one paired arrangement, repeating the materials and craft note's dimensions, material IDs, thicknesses and finishes, with the two printed phrases
5. Two connection drawings: one mounting and carrier-exchange overview for both modules on P and C; one enlarged detachable-link drawing with attached, released and paired rear views
6. Four adult wearing boards: W01, D1+D2 on a left wool-jacket lapel, 2.4 mm fabric, P; W02, D1 alone on a scarf edge, 0.8 mm, C; W03, D2 alone on a right wool-jacket lapel, 2.4 mm, P; W04, D1+D2 on a shirt placket, 1.0 mm, C
7. One 10-second connection video showing the selected pair's link attachment and release, followed by its W01 and W04 wearing states
8. One presentation document of at least 8 pages, with the selected direction and two printed phrases on the cover, reusing the direction comparison, selection, materials and craft note, final drawings, wearing boards and video stills

Acceptance:
- The three direction boards precede the selection note; the note names one direction, and the materials and craft note, final system drawing, connection drawings, wearing boards, video and presentation develop that selection.
- The materials and craft note, final system drawing and presentation repeat identical actual dimensions, material IDs, sheet thicknesses and finish allocations. Each module remains within 35 × 35 × 4 mm, the pair within 70 × 45 × 4 mm, and the decorative materials are M1 at 1.0 mm and/or M2 at 2.0 mm.
- The two connection drawings show two 2.4 mm clearance holes per module at 12 mm centres, C's 28 × 8 mm footprint, P's 7 mm and C's 9 mm rear projections, screwdriver access and the functioning spaces around the catch, jaw and pads. The paired rear view identifies one carrier and the module supported through the link, with mounting holes clear of the other module's material.
- The four wearing boards match W01–W04, label their W number, configuration, carrier and fabric thickness, and each include a reverse/contact inset. Their geometry, finishes and scale follow the final system drawing and the garments in wearer-wardrobe.png.
- The 10-second video uses the modules and link from the final drawings, shows attachment and release by hand, and labels its W01 and W04 wearing states with their carrier IDs and fabric thicknesses.
- The final system drawing and presentation cover print MODULE / MORNING and Two modules, shifting positions. The presentation contains at least 8 pages and reuses the named earlier work, including the selected direction on its cover.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
